1.title: Cohort composition, data availability, and prediction endpoints.
1.text: (Top left) Cancer-type distribution among patients with cancer-type annotations and clinical text; counts and percentages use the same cohort denominator. Other combines less frequent cancer types. (Top right) Major cancer-stage distribution among patients with a recognized stage (I-IV). (Bottom left) Cumulative cohort selection as successive data-availability criteria are applied; each box is a subset of the preceding box. Repeated counts indicate criteria without additional attrition. PRS, polygenic risk scores; somatic, somatic genomic features. (Bottom right) Numbers of available prediction endpoints in the mortality/metastasis, three-character ICD-10, four-character ICD-10, and PhecodeX schemes. Endpoint counts are not patient counts, and related endpoints across coding schemes are not mutually exclusive. Panel-specific denominators are shown in the artwork.

2.title: Discrimination and survival stratification using clinical text.
2.text: (Top left) Held-out Harrell's concordance index (C-index) for the base model, containing age, sex, and cancer type, versus the model additionally incorporating clinical-text embeddings. Each point represents an endpoint; the diagonal indicates equal discrimination. (Top right) Endpoint-level differences in C-index (text minus base), grouped by outcome scheme. Positive values favor the text model. Diamonds and bars indicate the median and interquartile range; violin densities are omitted for groups with fewer than ten endpoints. Endpoint counts are shown above each group. Endpoints are correlated, so these summaries are descriptive. (Bottom left and bottom right) Kaplan-Meier estimates of overall survival from first treatment in the known-stage cohort, stratified by major cancer stage (Bottom left) or quartiles of the text-derived mortality-risk score (Bottom right). Quartiles are defined across this cohort, with Q1 the lowest and Q4 the highest risk. Shading denotes pointwise 95% confidence intervals. Displayed C-indices describe the corresponding stage or risk-score predictor. P values in the bottom panels are from log-rank tests. ICD-10, International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision.

3.title: Relative predictive performance and joint associations across data modalities.
3.text: (Top left) Points indicate mean within-endpoint C-index ranks (1 = best); horizontal bars indicate interquartile ranges across endpoints. Ranking requires complete modality-performance results and is restricted to endpoints represented in the joint Cox analysis; its endpoint count may therefore be smaller than in the other panels. (Top right) Numbers of endpoints with a significant modality coefficient in the unpenalized joint Cox model. Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment is applied across modalities within each endpoint; significance is defined as false discovery rate below 0.05. (Bottom) Distributions of joint Cox coefficients per one-standard-deviation increase in each modality's risk score. Positive coefficients indicate higher hazard conditional on the other modality scores. Points represent endpoints; diamonds and bars indicate the median and interquartile range. For display in the bottom panel, coefficients outside 1.5 interquartile ranges of the first and third quartiles are omitted separately for each modality; displayed counts are reported. The top-right and bottom panels use the same joint-model endpoint set before display trimming. Endpoints are correlated; summaries across endpoints are descriptive. PRS, polygenic risk scores; met. burden, metastatic burden.

4.title: Mortality-risk dynamics and survival across cancer stages.
4.text: (Top left) Longitudinal text-derived mortality-risk scores standardized within each observation month; colors are truncated at z = -2.5 and +2.5. Rows represent patients and columns represent months. Up to 500 patients per dynamics group are displayed, with shown/full cohort sizes labeled. Falling, stable, and rising groups are ordered by mean fitted risk-score slope. (Top right) Kaplan-Meier overall survival by dynamics group, conditional on survival to the indicated landmark. (Bottom left) Dynamics-group proportions among patients with each recognized stage and an assigned group. (Bottom right) Conditional overall survival for stage I-II patients with rising risk versus stage IV patients with falling risk. In the right-hand panels, shading denotes pointwise 95% confidence intervals, and group-comparison P values use Cox score tests with delayed entry at the landmark. Panel denominators differ with trajectory, survival, and stage-data availability.
